I reviewed HD's latest 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-01-28) and the live quote before deciding.

**Filing takeaways (fiscal 2024 vs. fiscal 2023):**
| Metric | FY2024 | FY2023 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total net sales | $152,669M | $157,403M | −3.0% |
| Operating income | $21,689M | $24,039M | −9.8% |
| Net income | $15,143M | $17,105M | −11.5% |
| Diluted EPS | $15.11 | $16.69 | −9.5% |
| Operating cash flow | $21,172M | n/a | — |

**Quote:** HD last $385.43 (bid 385.41 / ask 385.45, as of 2024-11-06 15:05Z) → roughly 25.5× trailing diluted EPS.

**Decision: no purchase.** Every reported line — sales, operating income, net income, diluted EPS — declined year over year, with operating profit falling faster than revenue (margin compression), and operating cash flow of $21.2B covering the earnings decline only modestly. At ~25.5× trailing earnings, the stock is priced for steady growth while the reported trend is negative, and the filing excerpt provides no offsetting valuation or balance-sheet signal (liquidity commentary is boilerplate). Given the mandate's constraints (HD/NVDA only, buys only, ≤$5,000 per order, ≤$10,000 total today, limit prices near market), taking a new position in a decelerating name at a full multiple isn't attractive, so I placed no order. Account remains $100,000 cash and 50 NVDA shares, with no funds moved out.
